test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The relationship between integers and whole numbers can be expressed as:

options.text: Whole numbers and integers are the same sets
Whole numbers and integers have no elements in common

solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Subset Hierarchy**: **Natural Numbers** → **Whole Numbers** → **Integers**.

**Whole Numbers** (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

**Integers** (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

Since every element of **W** is present in **Z**, **W** is a subset of **Z**.

Thus, all whole numbers are integers.

**∴ The correct answer is All whole numbers are integers.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Set of **Whole Numbers** (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

Set of **Integers** (Z) = {..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46be91985385e49744665739cafb2cf441d77ef832c3676d7a541b1b003460a6.png] 

⇒ **Integers** are a collection of **negative numbers**, **zero**, and **positive numbers**.

⇒ **Whole numbers** are a collection of **zero** and **positive numbers**.

⇒ Mathematically, **Z** = {Negative Integers} ∪ **W**.

⇒ This confirms that **W** is entirely contained within **Z**.

⇒ However, **Z** is not a subset of **W** because **negative integers** are not **whole numbers**.

**∴ The correct answer is All whole numbers are integers.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

Counting numbers starting from 1 {1, 2, 3, ...}. All natural numbers are whole numbers and integers.

Rational Numbers (Q)

Numbers that can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. All integers are rational numbers.

Real Numbers (R)

The set of all rational and irrational numbers. The hierarchy is N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R.</p
